changes: No substantive changes. Added notes on the 'dāsa' name-ending, the reading of 'mukāmakā', and the unverified weekday.

date.as_written: saṃvat 1704 sa(?) caitra sudī || 12 || vāra ravīvāsare

notes: The scribe calls himself an inhabitant of Kāśī (kāsī vāsī) and wrote the copy 'near Śrībhīmasenī' (probably a Bhīmasena shrine or locality; not identified). 'mukāmakā (?)' is probably Hindi/Nepali mukām 'halting place, stay', meaning a temporary place of writing, not a separate place name. In 'Nārāyaṇadāsa', -dāsa is treated as part of the personal name (a Vaiṣṇava name-ending), not as a title. The era is taken as VS from the bare 'saṃvat' and the North-Indian (Kāśī) scribe. VS 1704 Caitra śukla 12 ≈ March/April 1647 CE. The Sunday weekday has not been verified. 'sa(?)' after the year is unclear (possibly 'samaye').
